text: You pay a fucking setter six hundred bucks a month, right?
style: Cheeky and mocking, quick, like a best friend about to roast you.

text: Plus five percent. Best hire ever, bro.
style: Proud and casual, a laid-back American guy bragging to his buddy, leaning back in the chair.

text: Cool, when did he answer your last lead?
style: Flat and deadpan, an innocent trap question.

text: She asked at two, he answered at five.
style: Shrugging it off, casual, like it's no big deal.

text: By five, she was in another coach's DMs.
style: Smug and slow, savoring the bad news, a tiny beat before the last word.

text: Six hundred fucking bucks for a reply three hours late? I'm firing him.
style: Shocked at first, the realization hits, then annoyed and decided on the last three words.

text: It's not his fault. Other clients, a life, sleep. Nobody lives in your inbox, not even you.
style: Calm and matter-of-fact defending the guy, listing the three things quickly, then a mocking jab on the last three words.

text: So I answer them myself, from his desk?
style: Defeated and a bit whiny, realizing it.

text: Nope, plug me into ManyChat. I answer while she's still in the chat, in your voice.
style: Smooth and sly, a quick 'Nope', then an easy, confident offer.

text: I hand those to your team, context included.
A hundred nineteen bucks a month, and I don't take five percent.
style: Smug and proud, a little beat before 'and I don't take five percent', a flex.

text: Okay, how do I set you up?
style: Hesitant and a bit sheepish, a small pause after okay.

text: Get out of his fucking chair, he went home like a normal human.
style: Mocking, laughing at him, slow and smug.

text: Comment SETTY and I'll send you everything to build your AI setter for free.
style: Smooth and smug, then warm and generous on the offer, like handing over a gift.
